extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, industry stakeholders, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), and apprenticeship system administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural requirements for development, approval, recognition, and use of National Occupational Standards, National Program Standards, and National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards, and the requirement for end-point assessments and Certificates of Completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation suitability for National Occupational Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship must be for an occupation that has been determined suitable for registered apprenticeship training by the Administrator pursuant to proposed § 29.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards are intended as resources to help set up new registered apprenticeship programs and keep existing programs current; they must be tied to an occupation deemed suitable under § 29.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: National applicability of work process schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The work process schedule framework associated with the occupation must be documented as nationally applicable (workable and applicable nationwide, not merely regional or local).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA will work with industry and stakeholders to determine national applicability; requirement ensures standards further growth of registered apprenticeship programs that meet national-level training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum framework for related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: National Occupational Standards must include a curriculum framework for related instruction that is documented or endorsed by relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula should remain up to date and reflect emerging technologies, work processes, and economic trends; aligns with ACA recommendations to update standards as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for evaluating apprentice progress, including end-point assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include methods to evaluate apprentice progress throughout the program, including development of an appropriate end-point assessment to assess attainment of required skills and competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must be nationally applicable and validated by industry; assessments should be transparent and accountable and can be used to analyze program effectiveness and drive continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive, industry-validated development process
rubrics_metrics.description: National Occupational Standards development should be intentional, proactive, nationwide, and industry-validated rather than a first-come, first-served reactive process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process should produce industry-validated curriculum for on-the-job training and related instruction, including interim credentials and industry-validated end-point assessments responsive to emerging labor force needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and finalization process for National Occupational Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OA will seek public comment on developed National Occupational Standards (including nationally applicable end-point assessments) for at least 30 calendar days and finalize standards within 90 calendar days from opening of the comment period (extendable at Administrator's discretion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA may specifically invite industry leaders to comment; Administrator may also consider data (e.g., O*NET) and other relevant information; the Administrator will maintain an up-to-date list of all National Occupational Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards: no conflicting licensing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: National Program Standards for Apprenticeship must be for training in occupations not ordinarily subject to differing Federal, State, or local licensing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because licensing requirements that differ across jurisdictions impede a uniform national standard, this criterion limits National Program Standards to occupations where uniform national training is practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards: national or multistate design, suitability, and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: National Program Standards must be national or multistate in their design, suitability, and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be demonstrated in multiple ways (e.g., a national/multistate employer, affiliates operating in multiple states, or national organization affiliations); ensures the program can operate across states without separate registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with proposed parts 29 and 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Any National Occupational Standards, National Program Standards, or National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards must satisfy applicable requirements of proposed part 29 and 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a baseline statutory/regulatory compliance requirement referenced across sections; submissions must meet these requirements to be approved/registered/recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator review timeline and written explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon demonstration that standards/guidelines meet established criteria, the Administrator will endeavor to approve/register/recognize submissions within 90 days of receipt; if declined, the Administrator will provide a written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 90-day target is stated for National Program Standards and National Guidelines and is consistent with proposed § 29.8 timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA reciprocity for nationally registered programs
rubrics_metrics.description: State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs) would be required to reciprocally approve and register programs that are registered via National Program Standards for Apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocity furthers system alignment by allowing nationally-registered programs to operate across states without state-by-state re-registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with existing National Occupational Standards and allowable deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: When National Occupational Standards exist for an occupation, National Program Standards and National Guidelines must use those standards; sponsors may make minor modifications provided submitted standards substantially align with the National Occupational Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable modifications include adding sponsor/employer-specific training, adding competencies or on-the-job training hours, or adding additional/academic-credit-bearing related instruction. Department requests comments on what deviations should be acceptable without undermining quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guidelines: national applicability and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards must be national in their applicability and scope with respect to the covered occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations of national applicability include having a national presence with local affiliates in different states or a presence in multiple states even if regionally concentrated; purpose is to create an adaptable template for local registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guidelines: suitability for local adoption/adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: National Guidelines must be suitable for use by state or local affiliates of the program sponsor (i.e., designed for adaptation and customization for local registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines are intended as templates to be tailored to local labor market requirements, collective bargaining agreements, and state/local laws such as licensing or ratio requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed local adjustments for certification and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: State or local affiliates using National Guidelines may adjust the template for local registration to meet state/local requirements (e.g., ratios, safety, occupational licensing requirements, different wage scales, contact information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department solicits comments on other acceptable adjustments; adjustments should enable local compliance while preserving core industry-validated elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic resubmission/recertification of National Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards must be resubmitted for approval upon amendment or at least every 5 years from the date originally approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification timetable aligns with general program review periods and aims to ensure guidelines stay current with changes in occupations, laws, or guidance; Department requests comments on timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and publication of approved standards list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will maintain an up-to-date list of all National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining a public, current list supports transparency and helps sponsors identify applicable national standards for program development and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessment and Certificate of Completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered apprenticeship programs must administer an end-point assessment at the conclusion of the apprenticeship term to establish successful attainment of all knowledge, skills, and competencies; an apprentice should only be awarded a Certificate of Completion upon successful completion of the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-point assessments should be rigorous, objective, and the culminating activity of the apprenticeship; they provide employers confidence in proficiency and help standardize outcomes across programs and industries.
